answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post locked collateral that is slashed whenever peers catch dishonest or duplicate identities. Because each fake persona demands fresh funds, mass fabrication grows expensive, and an attacker's balance sinks to its nadir as the slashes compound. Trust instead grows slowly and visibly, like a willow rooting into the locked timber of provable stake, so cheap sockpuppets can never buy their way into the network's trust graph.
